children: Nifty IT rises 3.02 per cent after TCS beats quarterly earnings estimates, while AI disruption and US labour curbs remain sector concerns

Indian IT stocks rallied on Friday, 9 October, after Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported better-than-expected second-quarter results, lifting hopes of a recovery in technology demand. The Nifty IT index rose 3.02 per cent, while TCS shares advanced 3.85 per cent to close at Rs 2,156 on the NSE.

The gains followed a prolonged correction in technology stocks, with concerns over client spending, artificial intelligence (AI) disruption and US labour restrictions weighing on sentiment. TCS’s results provided a fresh catalyst for buying, although a single session’s gains do not establish a sustained recovery across the sector.

TCS shares rose as much as 6 per cent during Friday’s session before closing at Rs 2,156. The stock had declined about 30 per cent over the preceding year, the steepest fall among Nifty 50 constituents, according to media reports. The Nifty 50 gained 1.3 per cent on Friday. The company reported consolidated net profit of Rs 13,884 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, up 14.9 per cent from Rs 12,075 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations increased 11.2 per cent to Rs 73,188 crore, compared with Rs 65,799 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26.
Valuations And Demand Remain In Focus

The rally also came after a difficult period for IT stocks. Attractive valuations helped support sentiment, while investors assessed whether the latest results signalled an improvement in technology spending. However, TCS’s quarterly performance alone does not establish that demand has recovered across the industry. Results and management commentary from other IT services companies will provide further indications of the strength and breadth of any improvement.

AI remains both an opportunity and a challenge for technology services providers. The sector faces questions about how AI-led automation could affect traditional services, even as companies pursue opportunities related to AI adoption. The implications for revenue and profitability will depend on how demand, pricing and delivery models evolve.
US Labour Restrictions Remain A Concern

The rally came amid scrutiny of US employment-based immigration processes, including the reported suspension of the PERM labour-certification process involving several technology companies. PERM is associated with certain employment-based green-card applications and should not be confused with a blanket suspension of all US work visas.

The policy developments remain a consideration for Indian IT companies with US operations. Their exposure will vary according to hiring practices, workforce requirements and the extent to which they rely on employment-based permanent residency applications. Friday’s market gains indicate an improvement in investor sentiment following TCS’s results, but do not establish that concerns over immigration policy or AI disruption have been resolved.

TCS’s earnings provided a near-term boost to IT stocks after a steep correction. The Nifty IT index rose 3.02 per cent on Friday, while the benchmark Nifty 50 gained 1.3 per cent. Whether the rally develops into a sustained sector recovery will depend on subsequent earnings, management commentary and evidence of improving demand across the industry.
